problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,3t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$

feedback.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩\cdot ⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =t(t+1){e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+0, \\  & =({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$
